stories.content:
The Malaysian government plans to draft the Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill for submission to the Cabinet in 2027 to regulate the data center industry towards more sustainable growth. The proposed bill was agreed at the National Economic Action Council (NEAC) meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday. The decision was made following a proposal on the National Strategic Direction Towards Sustainable Data Centre Development by the Ministry of Digital.

Essentially, the bill aims to ensure investments add value to the domestic economy, address water and electricity constraints while minimizing environmental impact, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir in a statement.

The lead ministries, namely the Ministry of Housing and Local Government, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry, the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, and the Ministry of Human Resources, along with the implementing agencies, should adopt the Circular Economy Framework (CEF) presented by the Ministry of Economy, Akmal added. The CEF proposes an integrated governance, monitoring, and coordination structure,

This could be Malaysia’s most important regulatory development for data centers so far, according to observers. Data center developers may eventually face more formal statutory requirements beyond existing task-force approvals and utility arrangements, they added.

stories.title_zh: 马来西亚经济部：政府正在起草法律以规范数据中心增长
stories.summary_zh: 据经济部称，政府正在起草监管数据中心开发的法律，作为实现行业可持续增长和向循环经济转型的战略方向的一部分。该法将为该行业的扩张建立正式监管框架。
stories.why_zh: 正式监管将使未来的数据中心审批与可持续标准挂钩，开发商需将资源效率要求纳入规划，而不能再将产能扩张视为不受约束。
stories.content:
KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 19): The government is drafting a law to regulate the development of date centres as part of a "strategic direction" to sustainably grow the industry and shift towards a circular economy.

The Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill is expected to be presented to the cabinet next year to tackle concerns about energy and water resources, and ensure investments benefit Malaysia's digital ecosystem, the Economy Ministry said in a statement on Monday.

The plan also aims to support Malaysia’s artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions and address environmental imbalances resulting from the industry.

The statement follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s call for Malaysia to plan the growth of the data centre industry to attract quality investments, strengthen the digital economy and ensure the sustainable use of energy and water while protecting the environment.

In a social media post earlier on Monday, Anwar said infrastructure readiness, energy supply and resource-use efficiency required closer scrutiny as the country pursued sustainable development of the sector.

Data centres now make up a tenth of Malaysia's energy consumption and this is expected go as high as one-third by 2035.

The government intends to make data centre investors to pay for the electricity grid upgrades they need.

Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani told Parliament last week that power for data centres would be unsubsidised and separated from the energy infrastructure for domestic homes and other industries.

This was to protect power generation capacity needed for other economic sectors.

A government task force on data centres had set that at least 30% of a data centre's components must be locally sourced, with greater participation in construction, engineering services, cooling systems and electrical equipment.

Up to July, the government has approved 27 data centre projects valued at an estimated RM225.97 billion, with 89.21% of the high-skilled positions to be filled by Malaysians.

Sustainable data centre development was among three strategic priorities reviewed by MTEN, alongside the circular economy and national economic resilience, as the government seeks to strengthen the economy amid structural challenges and global uncertainties.

The Economy Ministry also said the Housing and Local Government; Investment, Trade and Industry; Science, Technology and Innovation; and Human Resources Ministries would be the lead agencies adopting the Circular Economy Framework.

The framework seeks to steer Malaysia away from the traditional “take-make-dispose” economic model towards one that extends the useful life of materials, reduces waste and preserves resource value.

It also aims to address fragmented implementation across ministries, prevent economic losses from the wastage of valuable resources and support the country’s ambition of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050.

The Economy Ministry said MTEN also reviewed the National Economic Resilience Framework (NERF), which is meant to strengthen the country’s ability to withstand external economic shocks, and agreed that further deliberations are needed.

stories.title: SC Capital and NeoAI Cloud partner on 40MW South Korea AI data center project
stories.summary: Singapore-based SC Capital Partners and South Korean AI cloud provider NeoAI Cloud have jointly invested in a 40MW AI data centre project in Pohang, South Korea. The project has also attracted government-backed capital, giving it public-sector support alongside private funding.
stories.why_it_matters: Government co-investment signals South Korea is actively courting private capital for regional AI infrastructure beyond Seoul, opening a secondary market for developers and giving investors a de-risked entry point.
stories.title_zh: SC Capital与NeoAI Cloud合作投资韩国浦项40MW AI数据中心项目
stories.summary_zh: 新加坡 SC Capital Partners 与韩国 AI 云服务商 NeoAI Cloud 共同投资了位于韩国浦项的 40MW AI 数据中心项目。该项目还获得了政府背景资本的支持，在私人资金之外获得公共部门助力。
stories.why_zh: 政府共同投资表明韩国正积极吸引私人资本建设首尔以外地区的 AI 基础设施，为开发商打开二级市场，也为投资者提供了风险较低的切入点。
stories.content:
SC Capital Partners, a Singaporean private equity and real estate investment company, in partnership with NeoAI Cloud, a South Korean AI-focused cloud infrastructure provider, has invested in a 40 MW artificial intelligence data center project in Pohang, South Korea. The project has also secured investment from government backed capital, providing public sector support for the regional AI infrastructure development.

According to a press release, the purpose-built facility is designed to handle high-density AI workloads and will feature liquid cooling technology to support graphics processing units (GPUs), including NVIDIA Vera Rubin. The data center has secured 40 MW of gross power capacity and is expected to be completed by the end of 2027. The facility would also combine high-density data center infrastructure with GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS) and AI platform capabilities to support global companies developing AI models and operating AI services.

“We are excited to complete this investment, which represents our continued expansion into digital infrastructure in Asia Pacific. The development benefits from strong underlying fundamentals and is well positioned to serve the evolving requirements of the digital economy,” said, Suchad Chiaranussati, Chairman and Founder, SC Capital Partners. “We remain focused on identifying high-quality opportunities, particularly in South Korea, where strong policy support for AI and digital infrastructure is contributing to a favourable environment for the sector, and working with experienced local partners to deliver investments that create long-term value for our investors.”

Jonathan Yongwan Jo, CEO of NeoAI Cloud, said, “The Pohang AI data center is envisioned to go beyond traditional colocation by leveraging high-density infrastructure space integrated with GPUaaS and AI platform capabilities to provide a high-performance foundation for global enterprises to develop AI models and operate services. Building on the successful delivery of this initial 40 MW phase, we plan to advance a second phase expansion of 260 MW and look forward to a continued partnership with SC Capital Partners.”

The project has received power approval and building permits, and construction is underway. It has also secured an anchor tenant, with additional interest in the remaining IT capacity. The investment expands SC Capital Partners’ presence in South Korea’s digital infrastructure sector, as demand for computing capacity grows alongside the adoption of AI technologies.

NeoAI Cloud plans to develop a second phase with an additional 260 MW of capacity, bringing the project’s planned total capacity to 300 MW.

stories.title_zh: 生态成局供货稳，"中国博通"直面十万卡集群大考
stories.content:
当AI大模型从万卡集群向十万卡级规模演进，算力的瓶颈早已不再是单卡的计算能力，而是节点之间高速、稳定、低延时的互连能力。作为算力网络的“交通骨架”，高性能互连芯片正从幕后走向产业舞台中央。

10月15日，在无锡举行的“数涌智现·互连未来”众星微品牌及全栈产品发布会上，发布了12款量产产品与系统核心IP，同时重磅发布了 PCIe 6.0 Switch 、800G多协议AI NIC、多模RAID芯片三款新产品。

会议期间，无锡众星微系统技术有限公司总经理郭二辉、众星微副总经理兼总工程师宁佐林、众星微副总经理兼产品市场部总经理于颢三位高管，从技术、市场、生态多个维度，拆解了AI时代互连芯片的产业逻辑，也勾勒出国产互连芯片从追赶到并跑的突围路径。

### 一、范式重构：面向十万卡AI集群

800G多协议AI NIC是本次发布的核心产品，在宁佐林看来，这款产品早已超越了单纯的速率升级，而是针对AI集群场景完成了范式级的重构。

相比上一代400G产品，800G带宽实现翻倍，更关键的是两大定制化突破：其一针对AI集群的通信特性，在芯片中硬化了拥塞控制、多路径调度、选择性重传等功能，解决大规模节点互算时的突发性高带宽数据通路需求，甚至针对国内头部大客户的专属协议完成了定制化开发。

其二是原生集成PCIe 6.0 Switch，这也是众星微在国内最具差异化的技术优势。集成化设计不仅减少了一颗独立芯片，优化了整板级BOM成本，更显著降低了链路插损、提升了信号质量，同时提高了系统集成度、缩短了传输延时。

作为硬件系统的“交通十字路口”，PCIe Switch是CPU、GPU、硬盘、网卡等部件之间通信的核心枢纽。随着AI服务器架构演进，单台8卡通用服务器通常需要4颗PCIe Switch，而进入超节点时代后，单个超节点的用量可达几十甚至上百颗，市场需求呈指数级增长。

众星微本次发布的PCIe 6.0 Switch，性能指标已达到国际先进水准，填补了国内高端PCIe交换芯片的空白，也为国产AI算力基建提供了核心支撑。

### 二、国产替代加速：从“可用”到“好用”的平替跃迁

国产互连芯片的崛起，始于客户真实痛点的倒逼。郭二辉分享了一个典型案例：某互联网头部客户的存储机柜长期依赖国外厂商的定制化HBA卡与Expander芯片，但海外厂商响应慢、定制化能力不足，合作过程始终磕磕绊绊。

众星微原本没有对应产品线，但基于客户需求快速启动定制开发，依托自有Expander技术协助客户完成扩展板设计，最终产品在性能、稳定性上完全实现进口替代，更凭借本地化服务能力实现了海外厂商无法比拟的响应速度。

这一案例正是国产互连芯片替代进程的缩影。郭二辉透露，截至目前，众星微互连芯片累计出货量已突破80万颗，2024年出货约5万颗，2025年增长至40万颗，2026年预计突破100万颗。这些数字背后，是一次次设计、流片、验证和产品迭代，也是客户与产业伙伴给予我们的信任。

政策层面，去年相关部委发布国产RAID芯片与RAID卡支持政策，国央企层面率先启动国产化替代；商业端则出于供应链安全考虑，主动将国产芯片纳入供应链体系，已有两家重要客户将众星微RAID卡列为首选。

在郭二辉看来，当前国产互连芯片正处于替代加速的初期阶段，未来将呈现幂律式增长而非线性提升。这种加速一方面来自政策支持的持续加码，另一方面则源于国产产品自身能力的不断突破。

当产品从“能用”走向“好用”，从单点替代走向全场景覆盖，客户的接受度会快速提升，进而推动整个产业的国产化率进入陡峭的上升通道。

### 三、算力释放的瓶颈：互连效率成核心竞争指标

当AI集群规模从万卡迈向十万卡级，互连技术的挑战早已不只是速率。宁佐林认为，下一代互连的核心目标，是降低每Token的经济成本，真正让算力得到充分释放。

他用高速公路网络类比：5个城市的高速路网与10个城市相比，复杂度并非线性提升而是指数级增长，单点拥塞就可能引发全域拥堵。大规模AI集群同样如此，拥塞控制与路由调度，是决定整个网络效率的核心难题。

除此之外，工程实现层面的挑战同样严峻。宁佐林透露，下一代交换芯片的功耗将达到2000瓦左右，相当于一台家用电磁炉的功率，在方寸芯片上解决散热问题是极大的工程考验。

事实上，当前大规模AI集群的实际算力释放率普遍不足50%，表现较好的也仅能达到60%-70%，剩余的算力都损耗在互连环节的延迟、拥塞与调度低效中，这正是互连技术需要突破的核心空间。

客户选型指标的变化，也印证了互连价值重心的转移。宁佐林指出，当前客户选择互连产品时，核心关注三大指标：面效比、延时与功耗。

面效比决定了单平面可承载的算力卡数量，网络层数增加会导致成本指数级上升；延时则直接影响计算效率，若路径延时超过计算延时，就会出现计算节点空等的情况；而功耗的核心是局部过热风险，芯片局部温度可达90-100℃，是工程设计的致命挑战。 不同行业客户的需求侧重点也存在显著分化。

于颢介绍，运营商作为第二大应用市场，对功耗要求很高，因为每一点功耗增量最终都会转化为运营成本；金融客户对数据安全要求极高，对产品质量、测试验证与落地案例的审核极为严苛；互联网厂商则系统能力最强，会从硬件到软件层定义细分场景，比如PD分离架构、存算一体等，对互连芯片的场景适配能力提出了更高要求。

### 四、全栈与生态：构建长期竞争力的底层逻辑

在行业普遍选择单点突破的背景下，众星微选择了全栈多品类的布局路线。郭二辉解释，这一策略首先是为客户创造价值：全场景产品可以省去跨厂商适配的时间，避免不同品牌产品对接时的兼容性问题，帮助客户大幅缩短系统部署与开发周期；同时，单一厂商负责全链路产品，也能避免跨厂商排障时的责任推诿，从底层解决技术对接难题，为客户提供一站式的问题解决方案。

全栈布局在内部也形成了显著的协同效应。郭二辉表示，多产品线共享底层IP，比如PCIe Switch控制器同时应用于RAID卡、PCIe Switch与网卡产品，一次充分验证后即可跨产品复用，不仅节省了研发人力、成本与时间，更保障了技术一致性与产品质量。尽管多项目并行对人力资源提出了更高要求，但整体研发效益反而高于单点布局，这也是众星微坚持全栈路线的核心原因。

生态建设则是互连芯片企业的必修课。郭二辉形容互连芯片厂商是“一家托两头”，一头连着CPU、GPU，一头连着硬盘、网卡等外设，两端都要完成适配才能正常工作。海外厂商凭借数十年的产业积累，新产品推出后上下游会主动适配；而国产厂商则需要主动去适配生态。

众星微摸索出了协议分析、抓包排错的自主适配方法，随着80万颗产品的落地验证，越来越多国产上下游伙伴主动加入生态，“破壁无界，协同演进”的生态格局正在形成。

支撑全栈布局与生态建设的，是众星微分布式的研发体系。郭二辉介绍，公司在全国布局8个研发中心，各中心人数从60余人到200余人不等，采用跨地域拉通的项目组织模式，比如一个前端设计项目会同时集结无锡、西安、深圳三地的工程师。依托“星云”研发管理体系，团队覆盖了从网络仿真、架构设计、软硬件开发到工程量产的全链条技术，形成了完整的技术闭环。

### 五、长期主义：穿越周期的技术布局与产业判断

面向未来，光互连是行业公认的下一代技术方向，众星微也已提前布局。郭二辉表示，公司当前重点推进电芯片层面的研发，同时以多元化合作模式联动上下游伙伴，覆盖驱动、解调、光芯片、电芯片等环节，既有能量产的合作伙伴，也有研究型机构，共同推进112G到224G、448G的技术演进。

量产节奏上，112G已实现落地，224G处于突破阶段，448G将是未来大规模应用的节点。宁佐林进一步补充，众星微坚持有所为有所不为，核心电芯片由自己研发，光模块环节则与业界伙伴合作，不会涉足薄膜铌酸锂、硅基微环等光芯片技术路线的选择。

面向未来算力硬件多元化格局，众星微在互连产品形态上同步兼容 CPU 与 NPU 两类算力载体，从国内产业现状来看，适配 NPU 集群的互连方案落地节奏相对更快、更具现实性。这种开放协作的思路，也与公司“不做一家独大”的生态理念一脉相承。

针对近期市场热议的“算力泡沫论”，三位专家也给出了理性判断。郭二辉认为，这一轮AI浪潮对千行百业的变革是真实且正在发生的，从芯片设计、飞机汽车研发到农业、工业，AI都在实实在在地赋能产业，资本市场的短期波动不代表产业基本面。

于颢也表示，国内大模型厂商普遍存在算力缺口，AI基建仍有很大发展空间，所谓泡沫更多是二级市场概念股的结构性波动，与实体产业的真实需求并不匹配。 对于未来的战略重心，郭二辉明确表示，智算互连是下一阶段的核心投入方向，覆盖下一代网卡以及Scale in、Scale up、Scale out全场景交换机。

市场层面，国内市场的国产替代率将持续提升；同时随着中国算力产业出海，众星微也在推进互连芯片的海外布局，跟随整机与系统厂商共同出海，从部件层面参与全球市场竞争，让国产互连芯片走向更广阔的全球市场。

从800G网卡的范式突破，到全栈产品的体系化布局，再到生态共建与出海布局，众星微的成长路径，正是中国高性能互连芯片产业崛起的缩影。在AI算力重构全球产业格局的当下，互连芯片作为算力网络的核心骨架，其重要性愈发凸显。

凭借技术深耕、本地化服务与全栈生态的协同优势，国产互连芯片正在从“替代者”向“共建者”转变，不仅支撑国内AI产业的自主可控，更有望在全球算力产业中占据一席之地。这场关于算力效率的竞赛才刚刚开始，坚持长期主义的技术深耕者，终将穿越周期，收获产业增长的红利。

stories.title_zh: PLN Batam：巴淡岛大范围停电与数据中心测试无关
stories.content:
Batam and Bintan’s widespread outage last Monday was not due to the operational testing of a data center, according to President Director of PT PLN Batam Kwin Fo as quoted by a local daily.

“The widespread blackout that occurred on Monday (12/10) on Batam and Bintan islands had nothing to do with a data center. The information that there is testing or commissioning for data center operations, and it requires a lot of power, is not true at all,” Kwin reportedly told reporters in Batam yesterday, after news that the outage was linked to a data center testing was widely circulated in the community.

He added that the data center in question is still under development and is not expected to be fully operational in the near future. And if it does start operating, the operational capacity would not exceed 10 per cent of the total capacity of the data center, Kwin said. The data center was not named.

PLN Batam is Batam’s electricity utility, a subsidiary of Indonesia’s state-owned electricity company, PT PLN (Persero). Its full name is PT Pelayanan Listrik Nasional Batam; and it supplies electricity in Batam and surrounding areas.

Kwin Fo emphasized that Batam’s long-term electricity supply for data centers has been catered for in PLN Batam’s planning.

“We do not have a deficit or a shortage of supply. Our power reserves are still around almost 20 percent. Batam’s electricity load is targeted to increase from around 930 MW to more than 1,000 MW. Therefore, we estimate that by the end of 2027, the supply capacity will reach 1,200 to 1,300 MW,” he said.

Currently, Batam’s electricity system has a supply capacity of 930MW, with a load of around 780 MW. Thus, the power reserve is still around 20 percent.

The growth of electricity demand in Batam has exceeded 15 per cent, much higher than the 3-4 per cent growth of national electricity consumption. “We estimate that in the 2027-2032 range, the load will increase by around 300-400 MW. There is a growth of about 30 percent. To meet the demand, PLN Batam is taking steps to add additional power such as building a new Gas Power Plant (PLTG) and a new Solar Power Plant (PLTS),” he said.

Additionally, PLN Batam plans to use a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) or a battery-based energy storage system to support Batam-Bintan electricity. stories.title: AMD unveils open Helion rack for agentic AI workloads
stories.summary: AMD has introduced Helion, an open rack blueprint designed for agentic AI workloads, featuring flexible CPU and GPU configurations and open software. The design targets hyperscalers and enterprises seeking lower-cost infrastructure for autonomous AI agents.
stories.why_it_matters: An open rack standard challenges proprietary AI infrastructure designs and could lower entry costs for operators building agentic AI capacity, intensifying competition in the data centre hardware layer.

stories.content:
Mon, 19th Oct 2026 (Yesterday)
AMD has introduced the Helion agentic AI rack, describing it as an open blueprint for rack-scale AI infrastructure based on an Open Compute Project design.

The launch extends AMD's rack-scale AI strategy beyond its existing Helios platform and targets workloads tied to so-called agentic AI, in which software agents carry out tasks such as code execution, workflow management and enterprise automation.

Helion is designed to let customers choose between CPU-only systems and mixed CPU-GPU systems, depending on the AI work being run. The blueprint supports both liquid-cooled and air-cooled configurations and is intended to work with open software.

One version of the rack uses 6th Gen AMD EPYC processors and supports up to 32,768 CPU cores. That setup is aimed at hyperscale users seeking dedicated capacity for agent execution while linking to separate model inference systems.

Another version combines EPYC CPU nodes, Instinct MI350P GPU nodes and general-purpose compute in a single rack. AMD said the design is intended for enterprise users who want one platform for different agentic AI tasks.

At the centre of the pitch is AMD's argument that agentic AI will not run as a single standard workload. Instead, the company is positioning Helion as infrastructure that can be tuned for different mixes of processing, power use and cost, while fitting into existing IT environments.

Dan McNamara, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Compute and Enterprise AI, AMD, said the company sees a need for a broader set of infrastructure choices as AI deployments become more varied.

"Agentic AI is not a single workload. It spans personal agents, enterprise applications, code execution and complex workflows, each with different compute requirements," said Dan McNamara, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Compute and Enterprise AI, AMD.

"To do that takes optimized compute and infrastructure that can adapt to different workloads. With AMD Helion, we are bringing AMD EPYC performance, open software and flexible rack designs together so our partners can build systems around customer needs and make efficient use of available power," McNamara said.

### Open design

AMD plans to contribute the Helion specification to the Open Compute Project, placing the architecture into a wider industry effort around shared data centre hardware designs. That mirrors its message that AI infrastructure should be developed through a more open hardware and software ecosystem rather than tightly controlled proprietary stacks.

Helion also includes an integrated token router intended to direct model calls from agents across frontier and open-source models. This points to a model in which customers may not rely on a single provider, but instead route workloads according to task, cost or other operational requirements.

Support statements from server makers and infrastructure suppliers suggest AMD is trying to build a broad manufacturing and integration network around the design. Comments came from Cisco, Dell, Hon Hai Technology Group, HPE, Lenovo, QCT, Supermicro and Wiwynn.

Jeremy Foster, Senior Vice President and General Manager, Cisco Compute, said: "Agentic AI is changing what customers need from their infrastructure. It's not just about compute performance, but how the entire system is connected, managed and secured. Architectures like AMD Helion, combined with Cisco's full-stack infrastructure capabilities, can give customers greater flexibility to deploy, operate and scale agentic workloads into their environments as their needs evolve."

Dell also framed the launch around customer choice and validation. "Dell PowerRack gives customers choice without compromise, and our support for AMD Helion Agentic Rack Reference Design extends that promise to the next generation of agentic AI. By combining AMD's rack-scale architecture with Dell's proven engineering expertise, along with the flexibility to extend deployments with Dell PowerRack for Networking and Storage, we're giving customers a complete, validated path to deploy agentic compute at scale with the manageability and reliability they expect from Dell," said Arun Narayanan, Senior Vice President, Compute and Networking, Dell Technologies.

### Broader push

The announcement comes as AMD seeks to widen its role in AI infrastructure beyond selling individual processors and accelerators. In related remarks on its rack-scale portfolio, AMD said Helios is moving into production, with customer deliveries, deployments and workload validation under way, and early systems running at OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle.

That matters because it shows AMD trying to compete at the level of complete systems design as AI buyers increasingly focus on power, cooling, integration and model orchestration alongside chip performance.

For hardware partners, Helion offers a reference design that can be adapted for different customer environments. For enterprise and hyperscale users, AMD is presenting it as a way to deploy agentic AI using existing infrastructure investments while adjusting the mix of CPUs and GPUs to suit particular tasks.

"AMD Helion provides an open, flexible foundation for agentic AI infrastructure. Wiwynn is excited to collaborate with AMD, bringing our expertise in rack-level integration and advanced cooling to help hyperscaler customers tailor systems that meet the demanding workloads, power requirements, and data center environments of the agentic AI era," said William Lin, President and CEO, Wiwynn.

stories.summary: Samsung will use TSMC manufacturing technology for Nvidia's next-generation memory chips, according to a Seoul newspaper report. The arrangement marks the first time Samsung and TSMC have collaborated at the manufacturing stage.
stories.why_it_matters: Cross-foundry cooperation between the two largest contract chipmakers signals how Nvidia's supply demands are reshaping industry rivalries, with implications for memory pricing and advanced packaging capacity across the AI supply chain.

stories.content:
The move marks the first time the two companies have worked together at the manufacturing stage

\[SEOUL\] Samsung Electronics will use TSMC’s 3-nanometre process to produce base dies for Nvidia’s next-generation custom high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, the *Seoul Economic Daily* reported on Sunday (Oct 18).

The move would mark the first time Samsung has worked with the Taiwanese contract chipmaker at the HBM manufacturing stage, according to the report.

Nvidia has asked Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron Technology to use TSMC’s process for Nvidia HBM (NVHBM) base dies, and sixth-generation Dram technology for its core dies, the newspaper said, citing industry sources.

NVHBM, unveiled in August, integrates Nvidia’s custom memory controller into the base die and is aimed at standardising implementation across multiple memory suppliers, said the company.

Samsung accepted Nvidia’s requirements after an internal review, but plans to retain its in-house production model for standard HBM and custom products for other customers, *Seoul Economic Daily* said.

It is also assessing whether its foundry could produce NVHBM base dies if demand exceeds TSMC’s capacity, the newspaper quoted an unnamed source as saying. REUTERS
